difficulty_reason: For morphisms f : X -> Z, g : Y -> Z and Z -> T of formal algebraic spaces over S, the induced comparison i : X x_Z Y -> X x_T Y is asserted to be representable, locally of finite type, locally quasi-finite, separated and a monomorphism, with the additional conclusions that i is a closed immersion when Z -> T is separated and quasi-compact when Z -> T is quasi-separated (statement lines 6836-6847). The proof exhibits the square in which i appears as a base change of the diagonal morphism of Z over T: general category theory identifies X x_Z Y as the fibre product of X x_T Y with Z over Z x_T Z along the diagonal (proof lines 6849-6856), so the three items follow by applying to the diagonal the chapter's lemma on the diagonal of a morphism of formal algebraic spaces (proof lines 6857-6859). The level is H2: short, but the reader has to recognise the fibre product square for the diagonal and see that closed immersion and quasi-compactness are exactly the diagonal's separatedness and quasi-compactness.
